set.hook: Arnaud Donckele's sauce-led three-star on the Bouillabaisse beach, open only in the summer months.
set.why: Donckele has held three stars here since 2013, and Gault&Millau, which made him its Chef of the Year in 2018, still gives the room 19/20 in 2026. set.hook: Fabien Ferré's three-star at the Hôtel du Castellet: a sea menu and a plant menu, each built on one sauce.
set.why: Ferré came to the Hôtel du Castellet in 2013 and spent about a decade as Christophe Bacquié's number two. When Bacquié left he reopened the room under its new name in 2023, and in March 2024 MICHELIN gave it three stars at once, making him, at 35, the youngest three-star chef in France. The 2026 guide kept them. Guests choose between a marine and a vegetable route, or the Symbiosis menu that merges the two.

set.hook: Éric Canino's two-star terrace at La Réserve Ramatuelle: Guérard's light cooking, olive oil not butter.
set.why: Canino trained under Michel Guérard, who made lightness a haute-cuisine idea, then under Guy Martin at Le Grand Véfour, and has run this kitchen for more than fifteen years. The second star came in January 2020 and has held through the 2026 guide. His all-vegetable menu runs from starter to dessert and wastes nothing: beetroot is cooked in seawater, its leaves fried for crunch and the peel turned into the dressing.

set.hook: The Bruno family's truffle house in open country outside Lorgues; every course is built on the tuber.
set.why: Clément Bruno, whom Gilles Pudlowski called the Bocuse of truffles, turned this farmhouse on the Campagne Mariette into a truffle table and held a MICHELIN star for decades. He died in late January 2025, aged 77; Alain Ducasse and Jacques Maximin were at the funeral in Lorgues. His sons Benjamin, in the kitchen, and Samuel, in the room, run it now, keeping the single truffle menu and giving the estate's vegetable garden a larger part.

set.hook: Quentin André's starred dinner room at Terre Blanche, in the pine hills above Fayence.
set.why: André worked under Pierre Gagnaire at Les Airelles, Le Balzac and Sketch, then became Christophe Schmitt's second at Terre Blanche and was named executive chef in September 2024. He cooks the hinterland rather than the coast: baby vegetables from Tourves, line-caught fish landed at Saint-Raphaël, poultry from Vidauban and local cheese. The room is open only from late spring to late October, at dinner, inside a golf resort.

set.hook: Alain Ducasse's ten-room abbey inn in Provence Verte, cooking from its own kitchen garden.
set.why: Nicolas Pierantoni grew up in La Celle and joined the inn when Ducasse opened it in 1999. Ducasse sent him to Franck Cerutti at Le Louis XV in Monaco, brought him back as sous-chef in 2006, and gave him the kitchen in 2016. MICHELIN removed the star in its 2024 guide; Pudlowski, who had just eaten there, wrote that he could not understand it. The menu still comes mostly from the potager and the nearby markets.

set.hook: The first table on Pampelonne, begun in 1955 as a film crew's canteen; still a de Colmont family house.

set.hook: The Le Ber family's wooden terrace over Porquerolles' Plage d'Argent, grilling wild fish since 1957.

set.hook: La Pinède, the Mas du Langoustier's pine terrace at Porquerolles' western tip; grilled langouste to share.
set.why: The Mas sits on the Pointe du Langoustier, at the far western end of Porquerolles, at the end of a private pine track. Guests come off the ferry and are driven out by the hotel's shuttle from the port or the village. La Pinède, its terrace, serves a Provençal menu built around the catch: soupe au pistou, a fisherman's basket cooked like a bourride, and whole grilled fish or langouste brought out to share.

set.caveat: Strictly seasonal and remote: the 2026 season ran late April to 27–28 September and it is closed now. Reached only by the hotel's shuttle after the ferry. Whether outside guests can dine at night is disputed between listings, so ask. The estate's former gastronomic room did not reopen in 2023 (Gault&Millau) and is not this table.

summit.title: Three stars, two stars
summit.story: The Var's top tables sit inside hotels, and two of the three keep summer hours. La Vague d'Or, on the Bouillabaisse beach at Cheval Blanc St-Tropez, has held three stars since 2013 under Arnaud Donckele and in 2026 opened only from 7 May to 10 October. La Table du Castellet, beside the Circuit Paul Ricard, went from no stars to three in March 2024, when Fabien Ferré, Christophe Bacquié's former second, was 35; it is the one that stays open into the autumn, until early December. La Voile, at La Réserve Ramatuelle, has held two stars since 2020 for Éric Canino, a Michel Guérard pupil who cooks with olive oil instead of butter and serves an all-vegetable menu.
summit.where: La Vague d'Or, Saint-Tropez; La Table du Castellet, Le Castellet; La Voile, Ramatuelle

seastar.title: One star along the coast
seastar.story: Along the Var coast, the one-star tables are vegetable-led rooms that cook with the local catch. Colette, at Hôtel Sezz on the route des Salins, has had a star since 2021 under Philippe Colinet; one of its two dinner menus is entirely plant-based, and the room closes in early October. Récif, on the roof of Les Roches Rouges at Boulouris, kept the star José Bailly won in 2019 after Alexandre Baule took over in May 2025; he cooks here in summer and in Megève in winter. Shanael, by the Toulon opera, gave the city its first starred table since 2001 in March 2026, and as a city restaurant it is the only one of the three that opens all year.
seastar.where: Colette, Saint-Tropez; Récif, Saint-Raphaël; Shanael, Toulon

inland.title: Truffle, garden and abbey
inland.story: Away from the beaches, the Var's serious tables cook from the hinterland's own larder. At Chez Bruno, in open country outside Lorgues, every course is truffle; Clément Bruno, who built the house, died in January 2025, and his sons Benjamin and Samuel run it. Le Faventia, at Terre Blanche above Fayence, has Quentin André cooking Tourves vegetables, Saint-Raphaël fish and Vidauban poultry, from late spring to 26 October. The Hostellerie de l'Abbaye de la Celle, Alain Ducasse's inn in Provence Verte, lost its star in 2024; Nicolas Pierantoni, born nearby, still cooks mostly from its kitchen garden and keeps two Gault&Millau toques.
inland.where: Chez Bruno, Lorgues; Le Faventia, Tourrettes; Hostellerie de l'Abbaye de la Celle, La Celle

sand.title: Lunch on the beach
sand.story: These are lunch tables on the sand, open from spring to autumn, where the menu is grilled fish and whatever the garden gives. Club 55 began on Pampelonne in 1955 by feeding Roger Vadim's film crew; the de Colmont family still runs it, the crudités come from their farm, and in 2026 it is open until 1 November. On Porquerolles, where visitors cannot bring cars, the Le Ber family has grilled wild fish above the Plage d'Argent since 1957, from April to 1 October. At the island's western tip, La Pinède at the Mas du Langoustier serves whole langouste to share and is reached by the hotel's shuttle; its 2026 season ended in late September.
sand.where: Club 55, Ramatuelle; La Plage d'Argent, Porquerolles; La Pinède at Le Mas du Langoustier, Porquerolles
